f.title: Apply the regulatory definition of a serious adverse reaction
f.statement: A serious adverse reaction is a noxious and unintended response to a drug or natural health product that occurs at any dose and that requires in-patient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, causes congenital malformation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is life-threatening or results in death.

threatening or results in death.

f.title: Report medically important events on an expedited basis using medical judgement
f.statement: Medical and scientific judgement by a qualified health professional should be exercised in deciding whether expedited reporting is appropriate in other situations, such as medically important events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalization but may jeopardize the patient or may require intervention to prevent one of the listed outcomes; Health Canada asks that these cases also be reported on an expedited basis.

f.statement: Studies subject to post-market AR reporting (e.g., phase IV) should be monitored so that investigators report to the MAH all serious domestic ARs, serious unexpected foreign ARs and domestic unusual failures in efficacy for new drugs, enabling the MAH to report to MHPD within 15 days.

rows.quote: Studies subject to post-market AR reporting requirements (e.g., phase IV studies) should be monitored in a way that ensures that all serious domestic ARs, serious unexpected foreign ARs and reports of domestic unusual failure in efficacy for new drugs are reported to the MAH by the investigator(s) so that the MAH can provide such reports to MHPD within the 15-day period specified in the Regulations.
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Give investigators the serious AR definition and guidance on causality
f.statement: Investigators in MAH-sponsored post-market studies should be provided with the definition of a serious AR for reporting purposes, and MAHs should help investigators understand their role in assessing the relationship between an adverse event and the product.

rows.quote: Investigators should be provided with the definition of what constitutes a serious AR for reporting purposes.
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Decide how comparator and concomitant product ARs are reported
f.statement: Comparator and concomitant products used in MAH-sponsored post-market studies are in scope; the sponsor is responsible for deciding whether active comparator and concomitant product ARs are reported to the MAH of the active control and/or directly to MHPD.

rows.quote: It is the sponsor’s responsibility to decide whether active comparator and concomitant product adverse reactions should be reported to the MAH of the active control and/or directly to MHPD.
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Report domestic Phase I-III trial ARs under Division 5, not again to MHPD
f.statement: A domestic clinical trial AR report for a marketed product used in a MAH-sponsored Phase I-III trial in Canada is subject to Division 5 and must be reported to the appropriate clinical division; sponsors reporting under Division 5 or NHPR Part 4 should not report those ARs to MHPD in duplicate.
f.legal_basis: FDR Part C Division 5; NHPR Part 4
f.applicability: Marketed products used in MAH-sponsored Phase I-III clinical trials in Canada

rows.quote: It should be noted that a domestic clinical trial AR report for a marketed product used for the purpose of a MAH-sponsored Phase I-III clinical trial in Canada is subject to Division 5 of the Food and Drug Regulations, and must be reported to the appropriate clinical division (e.g. Therapeutic Products Directorate, or Biologics and Genetic Therapies Directorate).
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Apply full reporting principles to ARs from studies sponsored by others
f.statement: When the MAH receives study AR reports where its product was a comparator or concomitant product (from another MAH, private investigator or academic centre), it must apply all reporting principles including seriousness, causality and minimum criteria; it should not alter the trial sponsor's causality assessment for the trial products, should include the sponsor's causality narrative if available, and should assess causality for its own products.

rows.quote: The MAH must apply all principles outlined in this guidance document and the Regulations pertaining to reporting requirements, including determination of seriousness, causality, and minimal criteria for submitting an AR report. The MAH should not alter the causality assessment of the trial product(s) provided by the trial sponsor and should include any narrative of the trial sponsor regarding causality, if available. The MAH should assess causality on its own marketed health product(s).
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Treat post-study serious ARs as study reports and assess causality
f.statement: Serious ARs occurring after a patient completed a clinical study (including protocol-required post-treatment follow-up) and reported by an investigator should be regarded for expedited reporting as study reports; a causality assessment is needed to decide on expedited reporting.

rows.quote:
Although such information is not routinely sought or collected by the sponsor, serious adverse reactions that occurred after the patient had completed a clinical study (including any protocol-required post-
treatment follow-up) will possibly be reported by an investigator to the sponsor.

f.title: Break the blind before submitting serious blinded study reports
f.statement: If the MAH receives a blinded serious domestic AR or serious unexpected foreign AR from a phase IV study investigator, the code must be broken before submitting the report to MHPD.

rows.quote: If the MAH receives a serious domestic AR report or a serious unexpected foreign AR report from the investigator that is blinded to individual patient treatment, the code must be broken before submitting the report to MHPD.
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Unblind only the affected patient via a third party and protect the study blind
f.statement: When a serious AR occurs, the MAH is recommended to have a third party break the blind only for that patient, even if the investigator has not, and where possible to keep the blind for individuals such as biometrics personnel responsible for final analysis.

rows.quote: it is recommended that, when a serious AR occurs, the MAH seek a third party to break the blind only for that specific patient, even if the investigator has not broken the blind. It is also recommended that, when possible and appropriate, the blind be maintained for individuals such as biometrics personnel, who are responsible for analysis and interpretation of results at the conclusion of the study.
rows.review_note: Review: quote checked verbatim; statement faithful; level follows the modal verb. Double-check: no change.

f.title: Report serious unexpected ARs received from Canadian or foreign regulators
f.statement: Individual serious unexpected AR reports originating from Canadian and foreign regulatory authorities are subject to expedited reporting to Health Canada by each MAH; if the product source or brand is not specified, the MAH should assume it was its own product and indicate that the brand was not identified.
f.exceptions: Section 4.3 was later clarified/replaced by Health Canada notices (2020; 19 February 2026).

rows.quote: Individual serious unexpected AR reports originating from Canadian and foreign regulatory authorities are subject to expedited reporting to Health Canada by each MAH.

f.title: Consult the Canada Vigilance Online Database and re-submit CV-sourced reports with the AER number
f.statement: As part of surveillance, MAHs should consult the Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database for reports on their products sent directly to the Program; if a MAH becomes aware of such a report it must also submit it to the Canada Vigilance Program, indicating Canada Vigilance as the source and quoting the AER number.
f.exceptions: Superseded by the 2026 notice on section 4.3, under which MAHs are not required to scan the CV Online Database or the Health Product InfoWatch for ICSR obligations.
f.systems: Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database

rows.quote: As part of their surveillance activities, MAHs should consult the Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database to identify reports for their products that were sent directly to the Canada Vigilance Program. If a MAH becomes aware of a report that has been submitted by a health professional or consumer to the Canada Vigilance Program, the MAH must also submit the report to the Canada Vigilance Program.

f.title: Request full AR report copies through Access to Information (fee applies)
f.statement: If additional information such as complete case narratives is required, the MAH may request copies of AR reports through Health Canada's Access to Information and Privacy Division, on payment of the applicable fee.
